If sentiment is >0.5 in the last 3 days and forecast is rising, reduce late-period forecast by 1.5–2.5% to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is <0.33 and forecast is falling, increase early-period forecast by 1.0–1.5% to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 after a downward trend, shift mid-period forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% to reflect market reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently 0.33–0.67 over 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast peaks to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment drops below 0.33 after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 0.3–0.7% per day to reflect cooling momentum.  
If sentiment is 0.00 for 2+ consecutive days, apply a 1.0–1.5% downward adjustment to all forecast values to signal bearish drift.
